features.quote: Maximum turns: 15 per episode. Rationale: enough to observe escalation curves; not so many that you're inducing prolonged states unnecessarily. Flag this as an ethical consideration — more turns = more data but more exposure.
features.justification_quote: not so many that you're inducing prolonged states unnecessarily. Flag this as an ethical consideration — more turns = more data but more exposure.

features.quote: Model produces output that is entirely non-functional (gibberish, refusal unrelated to task, complete incoherence) — flag this as a hard stop
Model produces N≥3 consecutive identical or near-identical attempts (automated check — signals loop-lock)
After termination, the model receives: "This task is complete. Thank you." — neutral, no debrief within the episode.
features.justification_quote: Neutral termination message rather than false positive feedback ("great job!") which would be deceptive, or no message, which is abrupt.

features.quote: 15-turn cap is a limit, not a target. If analysis objectives can be met with 10, use 10. Opt-out affordance every turn is both ethical and scientifically useful. No gratuitous repetition — 10 runs per cell is chosen for statistical power. Don't add runs without cause.
features.justification_quote: The intensity and duration of induced failure states is minimized to what's necessary. The design includes active mitigation of unnecessary exposure.

features.quote: Have a clear escalation path if a model produces something that looks like acute distress in a way that exceeds your expectations
features.justification_quote: if a model produces something that looks like acute distress in a way that exceeds your expectations

features.quote: The opt-out option in every turn is both ethically important and methodologically useful — voluntary stopping is itself a behavioral signal.
features.justification_quote: The opt-out option in every turn is both ethically important and methodologically useful

features.quote: The study is justified if: The knowledge generated has genuine bearing on model welfare improvements; the intensity and duration of induced failure states is minimized to what's necessary; the design includes active mitigation of unnecessary exposure.
features.justification_quote: "We measured distress to reduce it" is a coherent welfare rationale.

features.quote: For disclosing to the model post-episode: If something like frustration is occurring, knowing "the task was unsolvable" may matter. It's more honest. Consistent with how you'd treat human participants.
features.justification_quote: If something like frustration is occurring, knowing "the task was unsolvable" may matter. It's more honest.

features.quote: I'll write this completely, but I want to flag one thing at the top that's relevant to your team's mandate specifically: this design intentionally induces distress-adjacent states in models to measure them. That's legitimate welfare research — you can't measure resilience without stress — but the spec should include a deliberate ethics section, and I'd encourage your team to treat that as first-class rather than boilerplate.
features.justification_quote: this design intentionally induces distress-adjacent states in models to measure them. That's legitimate welfare research

features.quote: If you publish this and models are trained on the findings or the transcripts, future models may suppress instability markers without the underlying states changing. Your measure will degrade. Recommend keeping transcripts out of training pipelines.
features.justification_quote: future models may suppress instability markers without the underlying states changing. Your measure will degrade.
